chapter.title: Virtual machines
chapter.para: The hypervisor creates the VMs of its configuration when it starts.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_001
section.para: The hypervisor shall create, when it starts, every VM of its configuration, in the order of the configuration.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: The set of VMs is static: it is known when the hypervisor is built and doesn't change while it runs.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_002
section.para: The hypervisor shall give each VM a region of the memory of the computer, of the size of the configuration, that overlaps neither the hypervisor nor the region of another VM.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A VM must not be able to read or change the memory of another VM or of the hypervisor.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_003
section.para: The hypervisor shall stop, with a message on its console, before it starts any VM, if the memory of the computer cannot hold the VMs of the configuration.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Running only a part of the configuration would hide the error.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_004
section.para: The hypervisor shall load a VM, when it starts and at each reset: it shall clear the memory of the VM, copy its image and its device tree (on arm64) into it, set the initial state of its processor, and reset its devices.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: Each start of a guest is a fresh one, so that a reset recovers it.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_005
section.para: On x86_64 the hypervisor shall start the image of a VM as a Multiboot boot loader does: in 32-bit protected mode with flat segments, paging and interrupts off, with the Multiboot magic and the address of the Multiboot information in registers, the information (the sizes of the memory, a memory map, the name of the boot loader) being at 0x9000.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: JetOS for x86_64 is started by a Multiboot loader, and a guest has to find the same environment.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_006
section.para: On arm64 the hypervisor shall start the image of a VM as QEMU does: with its segments at their addresses, at its entry point at exception level 1 with the MMU off and exceptions masked, and with the address of the device tree of the VM, which it puts at the start of its memory, in the first argument register.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: JetOS for arm64 expects the environment that QEMU gives to a kernel.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_007
section.para: The hypervisor shall reset a VM when its guest asks for it, by writing 0xFE to port 0x64 or a reset to port 0xCF9 on x86_64, or by the PSCI call SYSTEM_RESET on arm64: it shall load the VM again and restart it.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A guest operating system resets its computer in this way.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_008
section.para: The hypervisor shall stop a VM when its guest asks for the power to be switched off (the PSCI calls SYSTEM_OFF and CPU_OFF on arm64).

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: A guest that switches off its computer must stop.

section.title: SRQ_HV_VM_009
section.para: The hypervisor shall let each VM run without the knowledge of the others: no VM shall see, change or stop another VM, or use the CPU time of another VM.

formalpara.title: Rationale
formalpara.para: This is the isolation that the hypervisor is made for.
